# terms.GroupSpecificTerm { #formulae.terms.GroupSpecificTerm }

```python
terms.GroupSpecificTerm(expr, factor)
```

Group-specific model term.

Group specific terms are of the form `(expr | factor)`. The expression `expr` is evaluated
as a model formula with only common effects and produces a model matrix following the rules
for common terms. `factor` is inspired on factors in R, but here it is evaluated as an ordered
`pandas.CategoricalDtype` object.

The pipe operator `|` works as in R package lme4. As its authors say: "One way to think about
the vertical bar operator is as a special kind of interaction between the model matrix and the
grouping factor. This interaction ensures that the columns of the model matrix have different
effects for each level of the grouping factor"

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**expr**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Intercept](`formulae.terms.terms.Intercept`) or [Term](`formulae.terms.terms.Term`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The term for which we want to have a group specific term.

<code>[**factor**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Term](`formulae.terms.terms.Term`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The factor that determines the groups in the group specific term.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

<code>[**data**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[scipy](`scipy`).[sparse](`scipy.sparse`).[csr_matrix](`scipy.sparse.csr_matrix`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The values associated with the term as they go into the design matrix.

<code>[**kind**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Indicates the type of the term. Can be one of `"numeric"`, `"categoric"`, or `"interaction"`.

### eval_new_data { #formulae.terms.GroupSpecificTerm.eval_new_data }

```python
terms.GroupSpecificTerm.eval_new_data(data)
```

Evaluates the term with new data.

Converts the variable in `factor` to the type remembered from the first evaluation and
produces the design matrix for this grouping, calls `.eval_new_data()` on `self.expr`
to obtain the design matrix for the `expr` side, then computes the design matrix
corresponding to the group specific effect.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**data**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The data frame where variables are taken from.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[**Zi**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[scipy](`scipy`).[sparse](`scipy.sparse`).[csr_matrix](`scipy.sparse.csr_matrix`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

### eval_new_data_group_index { #formulae.terms.GroupSpecificTerm.eval_new_data_group_index }

```python
terms.GroupSpecificTerm.eval_new_data_group_index(data)
```

Evaluate the grouping factor as indices for new data.

Unlike [eval_new_data](`formulae.terms.GroupSpecificTerm.eval_new_data`), this method
preserves the distinction between
missing values and unseen, non-missing levels. Existing factor columns are
represented by their fitted index, missing values by `-1`, and unseen
levels by consecutive indices after the fitted columns.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**data**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The data frame where factor values are taken from.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[**index**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[numpy](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   One-dimensional `int64` array. Existing groups use indices in `0..G-1`, missing groups use `-1`, and new groups use `G..`.

<code>[**new_groups**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   New, non-missing levels in first-occurrence order. Interaction levels are represented as tuples of their component values.
